# `set_wheel_unidirection`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set the wheel unidirectional-movement flag; in firmware 9.31 it always fails and applies nothing.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER / established (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | A |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xceb30, SetWheelUnidirection @0x3017e0 (64-bit build) |

Requires a boolean (or integer, nonzero is true) as a bare scalar or first array element; missing, empty, null or wrong type gives 106. The parsed value is ignored in both builds: the backend only tests wheel state and returns an error. The handler has a result-0 branch that is unreachable, so every valid request gets an error: 318 when no wheel is selected, 203 while the movement thread runs, otherwise 210.

Side effects: Reads the selected wheel and movement-thread state under a lock and sets the thread-local error; the direction is never applied. No logger, setting write or worker start in the inspected path.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_wheel_unidirection"`. [READ] |
| `params` | boolean\|integer\|array | yes | - | Unidirection flag as a bare boolean or integer (nonzero is true), or the first element of an array. Parsed and then ignored. No default. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 106 | Parameter missing, empty, null, or neither boolean nor integer | `expected bool param` |
| 318 | No wheel selected | `device not connected` |
| 203 | Wheel movement thread is running | `equipment is moving` |
| 210 | Wheel selected and idle (the usual reply) | `not supported` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Because the method always errors, no reply_success example exists.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":81,"method":"set_wheel_unidirection","params":true}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_wheel_unidirection","error":"not supported","code":210,"id":81}
```
